chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from one who heard Abā Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying:

When death came to al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), he wept. So it was said to him, "O son of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), do you weep while you hold such a station with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and he said about you what he said, and you performed hajj twenty times on foot, and you divided your wealth three times, even sandal for sandal?" He said, "I only weep for two qualities: the terror of the point of arrival and the separation from loved ones."

key_terms.الْمُطَّلَعِ: the place or moment of ascent/arrival upon the next stage, i.e. what one comes to after death
key_terms.الْوَفَاةُ: death; the moment of passing from this world
key_terms.حَجَجْتَ: you performed hajj; completed the pilgrimage
key_terms.قَاسَمْتَ: you divided equally; shared out your wealth in halves
key_terms.مَاشِيًا: walking; on foot as an act of devotion

ai.seo_question: Why did al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) weep at the time of his death despite his great virtue?
ai.summary: This report describes the final moments of al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) and his weeping at the approach of death despite his lofty status and great deeds. He explains that his tears are due to the awe of what lies ahead and the pain of parting from loved ones, highlighting humility before the Hereafter.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Husayn Bin Is’haq, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from the one who heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘When the death presented itself to Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> wept. So it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> are weeping and your<sup>asws</sup> status from Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> which you<sup>asws</sup> are with, and he<sup>saww</sup> has said regarding you<sup>asws</sup> what he<sup>saww</sup> said, and you<sup>asws</sup> have performed Hajj twenty Pilgrimages walking, and you<sup>asws</sup> have distributed your<sup>asws</sup> wealth three times, step by step’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, I<sup>asws</sup> weep for two reasons – for the fear of Hereafter (for my<sup>asws</sup> Shias) and the separation from the loved ones’.
en.sarwar: Al-Hassan ibn Ali (a.s.) was born in the month of Ramadan in the year that the battle of Badr took place, the second year after Hijra (AH) (migration of the Holy Prophet (s.a) from Makka to Madina). It is also narrated that he was born in the third year. He passed away in the end of the month of Safar in the year forty nine AH. He lived for forty seven years and a few months.
His mother was Fatima, daughter of the Messenger of Allah.
